quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on a straight road:

options.text: You can usually keep control of the motorcycle.
You will likely lose control of the motorcycle.
You must release the rear brake to regain control.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually keep control of the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while you stop on a straight road, you can keep it locked until you stop completely. A locked rear wheel on an upright motorcycle going straight usually does not cause loss of control.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull to the side of the road until the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Rain makes the oily center of the lane very slippery. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars instead. The left tire track is usually the safest place to ride.

questions.question: A motorized scooter can be operated:

options.text: Only during the day.
Without a driver license.
With any class of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: With any class of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, anyone with any class of driver license can operate a motorized scooter.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Increase your speed.
Increase your following distance.
Decrease your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: To stay safe at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road. Be ready to change your lane position at any time.

questions.question: When riding during the day, you should wear:

options.text: Clothing with reflective material.
A short-sleeved shirt.
Dark-colored clothing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clothing with reflective material.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear reflective clothing even in daylight so other drivers can see you. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs.

questions.question: Alcohol reaches the brain ________ being consumed.

options.text: within minutes of
about an hour after
about two hours after

questions.correctAnswerText: within minutes of
questions.explanation: Alcohol reaches the brain and affects your riding ability within minutes of drinking it. Driving any motor vehicle while under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Use your mirrors when stopping at an intersection to:

options.text: Check if drivers behind you see you stopping.
Watch for pedestrians ahead.
Look for dark clouds that show bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check if drivers behind you see you stopping.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors to see if vehicles behind you notice you are stopping. Make sure drivers approaching from behind are paying attention to your actions.

questions.question: When you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you should:

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait for the emergency vehicle to move.
Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.
Never hold onto the rider.
Not lean into any turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to hold firmly onto your hips, waist, or belt. Passengers can also use secure handholds if available.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection:

options.text: Takes only a few minutes.
Takes about an hour.
Should only be done by a certified mechanic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Takes only a few minutes.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-ride inspection before every ride. It usually takes just a few minutes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn
No U-turn
No right turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It is white with red and black markings. It tells you that right turns are not allowed here.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, your feet should be:

options.text: On the footrests for balance.
Pointed with your toes aiming downward.
Relaxed.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the footrests for balance.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests while riding. Do not point your toes downward. They could get caught between the road and the footrests.

questions.question: Hearing protection:

options.text: Is not needed when the rider is wearing a helmet.
Is only recommended for long trips.
Should be used on all rides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used on all rides.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet on. Use hearing protection every time you ride.

questions.question: The safest part of the lane:

options.text: Is always the left portion of the lane.
Is always the right portion of the lane.
Changes depending on the situation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes depending on the situation.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position for all situations. Change your position based on what is happening around you.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle while carrying a passenger, you should:

options.text: Ride a little faster than you normally would.
Start slowing earlier than you normally would.
Merge into smaller gaps of traffic than you normally would.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing earlier than you normally would.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. The extra weight makes the motorcycle slower to respond. It takes longer to stop, speed up, and turn. Slow down earlier when stopping and look for larger gaps when entering traffic.

questions.question: The human body removes alcohol at a rate of:

options.text: About one drink per hour.
About two drinks per hour.
About three drinks per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: About one drink per hour.
questions.explanation: Most people remove about one drink per hour from their body. This varies by person. The safest choice is not to ride after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Avoid making sudden moves, as doing so could cause a skid.
Travel on the shoulder to be out of the way of traffic.
Use only the rear brake because the front brake is ineffective on slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid making sudden moves, as doing so could cause a skid.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, sudden changes in speed or direction can cause a skid. Be smooth when you speed up, shift gears, turn, or brake.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
Only stop to yield to other traffic.
Vehicles will be entering the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop. Yield to all crossing traffic and pedestrians. Then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When attempting to pass another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Ride within the posted speed limits.
Exceed the posted speed limit to complete the pass, but not by more than 10 mph.
Pass more than one vehicle at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride within the posted speed limits.
questions.explanation: All passes must be done within the speed limit. Pass only where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:

options.text: Use both brakes.
Use the front brake only.
Use the rear brake only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. This helps you brake quickly and safely.

questions.question: Why should a motorcyclist not rely only on mirrors?

options.text: Mirrors can get dirty and block your view.
Mirrors are never reliable.
Motorcycles have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots.
questions.explanation: Mirrors alone are not enough to stay aware of your surroundings. Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle.

questions.question: How should a motorcycle be parked on the road?

options.text: At an angle of 45 to 90 degrees to the curb.
Without any wheel or fender touching the curb.
Parallel to the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: At an angle of 45 to 90 degrees to the curb.
questions.explanation: When parked on the road, a motorcycle should be at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees to the curb. At least one wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
It automatically brakes based on your riding habits.
It applies the brake when you downshift gears.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems. When you press the rear brake pedal, it activates both the front and rear brakes together. Check your owner's manual to learn how your motorcycle's braking system works.

questions.question: Where are you most likely to have a collision?

options.text: At an intersection.
When riding in a group.
On the expressway.

questions.correctAnswerText: At an intersection.
questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest risk of conflicts between you and other vehicles.

questions.question: Where do most motorcycle and car accidents happen?

options.text: At intersections.
On the open road.
In parking lots.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle and car accidents happen at intersections. Usually, the car driver fails to give the right-of-way to the motorcycle rider.
